landing_note: 🔴 EVERY OA AGGREGATOR SAID CLOSED, AND ALL OF THEM WERE WRONG. Unpaywall (is_oa false, oa_status closed, zero oa_locations), OpenAlex (is_oa false, two non-OA locations), Semantic Scholar (openAccessPdf status CLOSED), Europe PMC (isOpenAccess N, inPMC N, single subscription-required fullTextUrl) and NCBI idconv ('Identifier not found in PMC') agree unanimously — because every one of them keys on the SAGE DOI record, and Experimental Biology and Medicine has since migrated to Frontiers. Crossref is the only structured source that shows it: its publisher field reads 'Frontiers Media SA' against a sagepub.com licence URL. The article is served free and complete at the Frontiers-hosted ebm-journal.org. journals.sagepub.com returns HTTP 403 (Cloudflare) on the landing page and on both Crossref TDM links.

skills_considered.reason: The acquisition was the hard part and this is the sanctioned cascade for it. Recorded in full because the result overturns what five OA indexes report: the win came at the open-web tier, on a Frontiers-hosted platform, after Unpaywall, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Europe PMC and NCBI idconv all returned closed or not-found.

Declined deliberately. This is a REVIEW. A claim-producing pipeline run over a secondary source is precisely how a review's summary sentence becomes a canonical datum, which is the failure D-15 in the dismissal ledger already records for this corpus. Read as a census of what its authors report instead.

Not triggered, and the trigger was checked rather than assumed. R4 is mandatory when a reading narrows, reverses, corroborates or removes a consolidated baseline claim, or justifies a MAJOR bump. This reading changes no claim's evidentiary basis: its dispositions are a registry promotion (Tier C placeholder to read) and a dismissal-ledger re-audit that STRENGTHENS the provenance of an already-reopened rejection without altering its verdict. If the ACK1 primary (PMID 16288044) is later read and moves DIS-001, that reading carries the audit.

No therapeutic lever matures here. The ACK1 lead is already held as an experimental probe under DIS-001 and is not a new candidate.

surface_preflight.text_layer_evidence: pdftotext -layout output carries 12 occurrences of 'þ' where the page prints '+' and 8 occurrences of the C0 control 0x02 where the page prints '−'. Every one of the 20 corrupted characters sits in genotype or receptor-status notation: 'WWOX (C3H)þ/\x02' for 'Wwox (C3H)+/−', 'WWOXþ/þ' for 'WWOX+/+', 'ERþ/\x02' patterns for ER− carcinomas. This is the exact defect class named in gold_is_in_the_details rule 5d, and it consumes precisely the load-bearing marks. A pymupdf re-extraction does not repair it — it drops the 0x02 entirely, so 'Wwox (C3H)+/−' becomes 'Wwox (C3H)þ/', silently losing the minus. Roughly 60% of the damage here is printable ('þ'), so a control-character screen alone would have passed 12 of the 20.
surface_preflight.consequence: The .txt is declared as article_text for provenance and is NOT used as the evidentiary surface behind any locator. Every body locator in this manifest is anchored to a rendered page crop under page_adjudications/PMID24510053/, whose recipe regenerates from the fingerprinted PDF. This is the first reading in this deployment to use the rule 5e remedy, which became runnable only when PyMuPDF was installed on 2026-09-09.
surface_preflight.column_layout_note: The article is two-column and pdftotext -layout interleaves the columns across the gutter, so a sentence read linearly from that output can splice text from two different columns. Reading was done from a column-aware pymupdf extraction (clipped left/right half-pages) used ONLY as a reading aid, never as a declared artifact.

group_assessment.weighting: 🔴 PRIMARY FOR THE GENE IS NOT PRIMARY FOR THE DISEASE, and here the split runs inside the paper. OBSERVATION: where this review recounts which Wwox mouse allele produced which tumour, it is reporting the group's OWN experiments (refs 13 and 14 are its own), so those statements sit close to first-hand and are weighted accordingly. INTERPRETATION: where it explains somatic cancer mechanism — above all the flat proteasomal endpoint it gives ubiquitination — it is a secondary reading of other laboratories' work and carries no more weight than the primaries it cites, several of which this corpus has never opened, including the ACK1 primary its own degradation section rests on. DISEASE: the group is not primary for the WWOX-DEE clinical phenotype and this article does not address that phenotype at all, so nothing here may be weighted as clinical evidence for the reference genotype.
group_assessment.research_type_note: The GROUP is experimental_lab — the Aqeilan laboratory generates mouse genetics and cell biology. THIS ARTICLE, however, is a minireview and produces no data of its own; the enum classifies what the group can produce, and the distinction between that and what this paper contains is the whole of how its statements may be weighted.

field_density.note: WWOX AND Ack1 returns FOUR records in the whole of PubMed. The degradation route this review names is one of the sparsest literatures touching the gene, and it is the one with a live, reopened rejection standing on it.

multihop.resolved_depth_declaration: 🔴 ONE RESOLVED, SIX IDENTIFIED BUT NOT PMID-RESOLVED, AND DECLARED AS SUCH. The 2014 reference list is author-title-journal-volume-page with no PMIDs and no DOIs, so resolution means matching by citation. I resolved exactly one, because it is the only one whose identity is load-bearing for this reading: ref 31 = Mahajan NP, Whang YE, Mohler JL, Earp HS, Cancer Res 2005;65:10514-23 = PMID 16288044, confirmed by esearch and esummary against title and journal. Its receipt status is an EMPTY list — never opened by this corpus — while it is the primary source of the ACK1-to-WWOX polyubiquitination cascade that active rejection DIS-001 turns on, and it already sits in full_text_queue_current.md. Refs 30, 13, 14, 15, 100 and 101 are identified by full citation in gene_direct_notes but were NOT PMID-resolved: none of them changes a disposition in this reading, and resolving a citation I am not going to act on would be work performed to look thorough.

entries.proposition: The review states its own remit, and the remit is oncology. It is a census of WWOX in cancer; it is not, and does not claim to be, about germline WWOX disease. Screened over the BODY with the 103-item reference list separated off first: zero occurrences of epilepsy, seizure, brain, CNS, WOREE, encephalopathy, ataxia, intellectual, recessive or syndrome, and zero of Q230 or SCAR12. The only two 'neuro' hits in the whole file are JOURNAL NAMES in the reference list ('Neuro endocrinol Lett', 'J Neuro-oncol') — back matter, not content, and exactly the contamination class registered as open item 3 of the receipt contract. Its single 'germline' mention is two germline mutations found in a somatic lung-cancer sequencing series.

entries.proposition: 🔴 THE REVIEW ENCODES, AS A DEFINITION, THE EXACT TEXTBOOK DEFAULT THIS REPOSITORY NAMES AS D-01. It defines ubiquitination as an enzymatic cascade whereby proteins are labelled with a ubiquitin tag 'and thus designated for degradation via the proteasomal system' — a flat universal, with no linkage determination anywhere in the paper, cited to ref 30, which is a bone-formation review carrying no WWOX linkage data. D-01 in the dismissal ledger's DEFAULTS THAT BIT US table is 'polyubiquitination → proteasome', recorded as FALSE as a universal because K48 commonly supports proteasomal turnover while K63 is multifunctional. The review is therefore a source-level INSTANCE of that default, not a resolution of it.

entries.proposition: The ACK1 route, and the provenance active rejection DIS-001 was missing. Ack1, an intracellular tyrosine kinase, induces WWOX polyubiquitination and subsequent degradation in prostate cancer cells; in human androgen-independent prostate cancer specimens, raised phospho-Ack1 accompanies reduced WWOX against benign tissue. The review's own modal is 'suggesting' for the causal step, and the primary is ref 31 = PMID 16288044, which this corpus has never opened.
